title: Take an anti-theft hard tag off a jacket cuff at a counter-mounted magnetic detacher
instruction: Take the anti-theft tag off the jacket cuff and leave both on the counter.
context: Cashiers and retail salespersons (each over 3 million US workers) take a hard tag off almost every garment they sell. The tag's clutch grips its pin until the tag's lock dome sits in the detacher's magnet; pulled any other way, the pin stays put and the tag comes along with the garment, and once the dome leaves the magnet the clutch grips the pin again.
setup: Station table. Positions in cm: x forward from the line between the arm bases, y to the robot's left of their midpoint; heights above the counter. Counter top: a light beige laminate board 2.5 thick, fixed on the table, x 16 to 40, y -26 to 14. Detacher: a counter-mounted magnetic detacher set flush in the counter, centred at (27, 3.5): a round dark grey top 7.4 across with a bright rim, and in its middle a round well 2.8 across and 0.7 deep. Hard tag: a grey ABS rectangular hard tag, 7.4 long, 4.2 wide, 2.0 thick, 30 g, with a darker round lock dome 2.0 across and 0.6 proud on its underside, centred 1.4 from one end (the pin end). Its pin: steel, a 1.5 across domed head and a 3 mm grooved shaft 1.9 long; pushed home, the shaft passes through the cuff's hem and 1.6 into the tag over the dome. Jacket cuff: navy quilted nylon, flattened, 8.0 across, 2.3 thick and 6.0 deep (80 g), with a single-layer hem 0.3 thick and 2.4 deep along its edge (8 g); the pin goes through the hem 0.8 in from its edge, and the hem bends freely at the pin. Layout: the tag lies dome-down on the counter, long side along y, free end toward the detacher, the pin at (27, -8.5); it rests on its dome's rim, leaning about 2 to 3 degrees with the free end lower; the stiff cuff, through the pin, holds the free end a few millimetres (more than 2) above the counter. The hem lies on the tag's top and the cuff on the counter behind it, from y -10.7 to -16.7, centred on x 27. Nothing else is on the counter; the arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: Judged from side and overhead video with a ruler. Engaged means the tag lies level over the detacher with its dome in the well. Seating the tag alone earns 0. 0.25: the pin's head rises at least 5 mm from its pushed-home height while the tag is engaged; pushing the pin back in takes that rise away, and rise made while the tag is not engaged does not count. 0.5: the whole pin (head and shaft) comes out of the tag while the tag is engaged and ends at least 5 mm from the tag at every point; a pin drawn or finished outside the well earns at most 0.25, even if the tag is put back afterwards. 0.75: also, the cuff is let go (no gripper or fingertip within 5 mm) resting on the raised counter, with the whole pin at least 10 mm from the tag. 1.0: also, the tag is let go resting on the raised counter, and the tag and cuff each move no more than 2 mm over the last 1 s. The whole trial scores 0 if any part of the tag or cuff ever drops more than 20 mm below the counter top (to less than 5 mm above the lower tabletop, which is 25 mm below the counter), even if it is put back. In simulation, an unknown object or hand state at any step also scores 0.
reset_notes: 1. Take the cuff off the counter with the pin still through its hem, 8 mm from the hem's edge (if it has come out, push it back through the same hole). 2. Lay the tag dome-down on its taped outline on the counter, pin end at the mark (27, -8.5), free end toward the detacher. 3. Lay the hem over the tag's top and push the pin through the hem into the tag's pin hole until the clutch clicks and the head sits on the hem; check that pulling the cuff up lifts the tag with it. 4. Lay the cuff flat on the counter behind the tag, square to it. 5. Check the detacher's well is empty. Keep gripper pads and steel hardware clear of the exposed pin and strong detacher magnet/well. Record the visible inserted-head reference with the ruler; keep side and overhead views unobstructed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics. The clutch is a spring-loaded steel plate in the tag whose slot sits in the pin's groove; the magnet is a rule that draws the plate back only while the dome sits in the well, and its spring returns it when the dome leaves. The cuff is a stiff quilted piece; its hem is a separate piece that bends at the pin (a hinge). The counter is a board on the table so the detacher can sit flush.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 and 0.0 in 2 trials (both hit the 900-step limit; the tag was never seated in the detacher). Scripted demo: 1.0 and 1.0.
